items.text: I can explain what EFS is and why it is different from EBS
I know EFS uses NFSv4 protocol on port 2049
I understand what a mount target is and why one per AZ is needed
I can compare EFS Standard vs One Zone storage classes and when to use each
I understand the two performance modes: General Purpose vs Max I/O
I understand the three throughput modes: Elastic, Provisioned, Bursting
I know EFS is Linux-only and FSx is needed for Windows
I can create an EFS file system in the AWS console
I can identify and configure mount targets and their security groups
I can mount an EFS file system on a Linux EC2 instance using NFS commands
I can add EFS to /etc/fstab with the _netdev option for persistent mounting
I can enable lifecycle management to automatically tier files to IA
I can delete an EFS file system and verify no ongoing charges
Multiple instances sharing same files → EFS (not EBS)
Windows shared storage → FSx for Windows (not EFS)
EFS port = 2049 — common exam troubleshooting question
Performance mode cannot be changed after creation
EFS Standard-IA reduces cost for infrequently accessed files — key for cost optimization questions
EFS One Zone = single AZ = lower cost but lower availability
